title: Helix TaskSet
description: plan/taskset.yaml: the scope, as Lane › Epic › Feature › Story. Each task names its story in `story`; its feature, epic and lane follow. YAML order is reading order only: the order work is delivered in is Helix Milestones (plan/milestones.yaml).

revision.description: 1 for the TaskSet as first planned; applying Helix Milestones adds one, and keeps the revision it replaces in plan/history/.

milestones.description: The Helix Milestones file beside it, milestones.yaml. Absent only in revision 1, before the milestones are planned.

timelines.description: The finish dates the loop's app shows: [code, project] (both, the default) or [project]. Project complete is when everything is done, human tasks and their lead times included; code complete is when the last builder task would merge if every human task were done when it is needed, so a wait for an account or a D-U-N-S number doesn't count against the build.

lanes.description: The repositories the loop builds, keyed by lane key. Every epic lives in exactly one lane.

repo.description: The repository the lane builds, as tasks name it in `repo` and the config declares it under `repos`.

epics.description: Large strategic outcomes, keyed by a key unique across the TaskSet.

title.description: Named for the outcome, not the code: "Social publishing", not "Publishing service".

outcome.description: What is true for people once the epic is done, in a sentence.

features.description: Deliverable capabilities a user would recognise, each a vertical slice, keyed by a key unique across the TaskSet.

capability.description: Optional: what the feature lets people do, in a sentence.

stories.description: User stories, each one need small enough to demo on its own, keyed by a key unique across the TaskSet.

need.description: "As a …, I want …, so that …" (or "As the …"): the person it serves, what they need, and why.
